articles.title: Trichotillomania: Boredom and tiredness outpace negative emotions as predictors of hair pulling
articles.summary: People with hair-pulling disorder often blame negative emotions for their symptoms. However, a new real-time tracking study reveals that boredom and tiredness may actually be more consistent predictors of future hair-pulling episodes than emotional distress.

articles.title: Sexually assertive individuals tend to be more satisfied with their relationships, study finds
articles.summary: New research from Italy reveals that sexually assertive individuals tend to be more satisfied in their romantic relationships. The study also highlights a positive connection between body appreciation, sexual esteem, and the ability to communicate sexual desires.

articles.title: Valhalla: A Layered Knowledge-State and Service-Governance Framework for Long-Term Scientific Knowledge Work
articles.summary: arXiv:2608.15193v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly adopted in scientific research, external knowledge bases, knowledge graphs, and long-term memory have improved information retrieval and task continuity. However, most structured knowledge systems remain node-centric, representing files, concepts, results, and judgments as nodes and relations in a graph. While suitable for personal knowledge management, such structures often depend on individual organizational practices, limiting knowledge sharing, integration, and reorganization across users.

articles.title: Medicinal mushroom supplements linked to a sudden relapse of psychosis in new case report
articles.summary: A recent case report suggests that over-the-counter medicinal mushroom supplements might have worsened severe psychotic symptoms in a young man with cerebral palsy, highlighting the potential psychiatric risks of mixing natural remedies with mental health conditions.

articles.title: Early antidepressant use is linked to higher levels of sexual boredom
articles.summary: People using common antidepressants for up to two years report higher levels of general and sexual boredom than non-users. This hidden side effect could explain why some patients struggle to stick with their mental health treatments over time.

articles.title: A therapy that “rewrites” childhood memories can ease fear of failure
articles.summary: Childhood criticism can leave people carrying a fear of failure long into adulthood, but new research suggests those emotional patterns may be surprisingly flexible. Young adults who revisited painful memories through imagery-based therapy showed lasting reductions in fear, guilt, sadness, and stress.

articles.title: Mindful partners use less hostile ways to say no to sex, study finds
articles.summary: Saying no to sex can cause emotional strain in a romantic relationship. A new psychological evaluation finds that mindful individuals reject their partners with less hostility, fostering better communication and higher overall relationship satisfaction.

articles.title: Scientists tracked kids for 8 years — the screen time result was unexpected
articles.summary: An eight-year Finnish study found that children who spent more time on screens tended to show better cognitive processing as teenagers, challenging common assumptions about screen use. Researchers say the key may be balancing physical activity with screen activities that encourage learning, creativity, and active thinking.

articles.title: A little-known protein may be fueling Alzheimer’s — and scientists found a way to block it
articles.summary: An experimental Alzheimer’s compound prevented damaging protein clumps from forming in the brains of mice, helping nerve cells survive longer and reducing amyloid buildup. The treatment also appeared to improve heart health and slow some signs of aging, raising hopes for an entirely new way to combat dementia.

articles.title: A little movement in midlife could pay off for your brain years later
articles.summary: Exercise and healthy blood sugar levels in midlife may help slow cognitive decline decades later. Physical activity appeared especially beneficial for Mexican American adults, suggesting that some brain-protective factors may differ across populations.
